about.heading: Not a topper. *A builder.*
about.subheading: Somewhere between dreams & reality — that's where I build.
about.bio:
I'm Aarav, a self-taught developer from Delhi, India. While the class was copying notes from the board, I was on the last bench sketching app ideas in the margins — and then going home to actually build them.

I design and build websites, web apps, Discord bots and small games, with a big focus on speed, clean design and the tiny details most people never notice. I don't talk much about what I'm building. I just ship it.

items.title: Nebula Dashboard
items.description: A real-time analytics dashboard with live charts, dark mode, role-based access and blazing-fast filtering.
items.details:
Built for a small business that needed to see their sales live. Charts update over websockets, filters run instantly on 100k+ rows and the whole thing works offline.

Stack: Next.js, Node.js, MongoDB, Chart.js.

items.title: Neon Runner
items.description: A fast-paced rooftop platformer that runs right in the browser — combos, coins and a global leaderboard.
items.details: A canvas game with custom physics, controller support and a serverless leaderboard. Started as a doodle in my maths notebook.

items.description: A football stats tracker with player heatmaps, goal timelines and head-to-head comparisons. SIUUU.
items.details: Pulls live match data, draws heatmaps on a pitch and lets you compare any two players. Yes, Ronaldo wins every comparison.

teacher.subject: PHYSICS — CLASS NOTES
teacher.title: Chapter 7: Laws of Motion
teacher.notes:
1. Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia): An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.

2. Newton's Second Law: The acceleration of an object depends on the net force acting on it and its mass. F = m × a.

3. Newton's Third Law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

Important: Learn all three laws with examples for the unit test on Monday. Revise numericals from exercise 7.2 (Q1 – Q15).

Homework: Complete worksheet 7B and submit before Friday.
